stories.headline: James, Embiid play 76ers' preseason finale, but 'still working on our rhythm'
stories.summary: Without VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday night's 125-120 loss to the Celtics, 76ers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what this team may look like this season, including LeBron James and Joel Embiid playing preseason highs in minutes.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- As the Philadelphia 76ers begin a season with a star-laden roster, center Joel Embiid rejects the narrative that anyone needs to sacrifice for this team to succeed.

"I'm against the concept of sacrificing," he said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."

Albeit without second-year starting guard VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday's 125-120 loss to the Boston Celtics for precautionary reasons, Sixers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what this Sixers team may look like this season.

The other active Sixers starters -- LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Embiid -- all played preseason highs in minutes and well into the second half. Embiid, who struggled in his last appearance two games ago against the Brooklyn Nets, finishing with six points and eight turnovers, was dominant.​

He scored 27 points, grabbed eight rebounds and added five assists. In the third quarter, he had one of the game's best highlights when he threw down an emphatic dunk that drew roars from fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena. "It's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again," Embiid said with a smile. "I guess I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed."

Still, the group never looked comfortable together on the floor, despite playing against Celtics reserves. After the game, players didn't shy away from their somewhat disjointed performance. Brown pointed to the team's spacing Friday night, which he said led to turnovers, as one of the many things they need to fix moving forward.

"We're not where we want to be yet," he said. "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day."

James echoed Brown's comments, but neither seemed concerned about the Sixers' ability to eventually jell.

"We're getting there," James said. "I mean, obviously we are a couple of weeks in, so we're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks, and it's not going to be perfect."

The Sixers open the regular season against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Rain postpones Game 4 of ALCS to Saturday; Rays, Guardians to play Game 5 on Sunday
stories.summary: Game 4 of the ALCS was postponed late Friday night due to rain, creating an unusual set of circumstances for the Guardians and Rays.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- Game 4 of the American League Championship Series was postponed late Friday night due to rain, creating an unusual set of circumstances for the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays as the Milwaukee Brewers await in the World Series.

Friday's game was rescheduled for 8 p.m. ET on Saturday. Game 5 was pushed to 5 p.m. ET on Sunday, which was originally a scheduled off-day.

Game 4's pitching matchup will remain the same; All-Star hurler Nick Martinez will start for the Rays, and reliever Shawn Armstrong will open a bullpen game for the Guardians.

"It never cleared out the way they were hoping it would," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "It started to get later in the hour, and MLB and I think both clubs did everything they could to try to get it in. Made the most sense at this point and this hour, with no guarantee that there wasn't another band coming."

The Guardians hold a 2-1 series lead after winning 3-2 in Game 3 on Thursday. The first pitch for Game 3 was moved up from 6 p.m. to 1 p.m. ET to avoid inclement weather in the forecast.

The teams would play Game 6 on Monday and Game 7 on Tuesday at Tropicana Field, if they are necessary. If the series goes seven games, the clubs would play four games over four consecutive days.

The winner of the series will face the Brewers, who will have a week off after advancing to the World Series on Thursday. Game 1 of the World Series is scheduled for Oct. 23 in Milwaukee.

"This is what we do," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "We play every day. Our guys get psyched or get cranked up an hour before game time. That never happened today. So, it was a pretty calm day overall.

"These are professional baseball players. They know how to get ready. They know how to get going. I'm sure the Rays are in the same boat. Tomorrow is game day. Hopefully, there's no weather. I know it's going to be cold, but we'll be ready to play tomorrow night at 8:08."

stories.headline: Dream's Angel Reese won't 'shy away' from big stage of WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Dream forward Angel Reese is embracing her first trip to the WNBA Finals with open arms, saying she's not about to "shy away from the moment" against the Valkyries.
stories.body:
OAKLAND, Calif. -- Angel Reese spent the better part of the past year manifesting a trip to the WNBA Finals. Now, she is just under 24 hours away from Game 1 of this year's championship series between her Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries.

In her first season with the Dream, Reese has had a career year.

Though veterans usually warn that the playoffs are a different beast, Reese has taken her production to another level in her first postseason stint.

"You have to be a playoff riser," Reese said at Finals media day Friday. "The greats are built for this. If you want to be considered the best player and well-respected, you can't shy away from the moment."

Reese is averaging 18.0 points, 8.4 rebounds, 2.2 blocks, 2.0 assists and 1.6 steals through five playoff games. The scoring and blocks have increased from the regular season, and she's shooting 38.5% from beyond the arc.

She has also been the anchor for the Dream's defense, which has been the best in the playoffs.

Although this is Reese's first time in the Finals, she's drawing on experience competing at high levels in college and with Team USA.

In September, Reese was a member of the gold medal World Cup team in Berlin. In 2023, she won an NCAA Title with the LSU Tigers.

"Anywhere I go, I am looking to win," Reese said. "I have won at every level I have been at. Coming into any situation, I have a winning mentality -- no matter what it looks like or what it takes."

stories.headline: Miami coach unbothered by Messi getting award in Spain 2 days before MLS game
stories.summary: Inter Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González confirmed Lionel Messi will travel to Spain next week to receive a prestigious award before rejoining the club for an MLS game two days later.
stories.body:
Inter Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González confirmed Lionel Messi will travel to Spain next week to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, before rejoining the club for the match against the New York Red Bulls two days later.

Messi is due to attend the ceremony in Oviedo on Oct. 22 ahead of Miami's MLS game against the Red Bulls in Harrison, New Jersey.

- MLS Power Rankings: Miami back to winning ways, as Nashville chase history

- Garber won't dish on exchange with Messi: 'Between me and Leo'

But González said he had no concerns about Messi's travel schedule ahead of the game.

"Yes, he does have this event [in Oviedo], and I love that he will assume it in this way. The whole club agrees that he should be there because it is a terribly important award, not just for him but for his family," González told reporters on Friday.

"Then, of course, I will count on him for the game [against the New York Red Bulls]. Leo has the possibility, not an advantage, and I said it the other day after the match, I want him to be good.

"He needs this. He'll be there, then I will have him at the game so I'm not worried about that at all."

The Princess of Asturias Award recognizes individuals and institutions for notable achievements in fields like literature, social sciences, scientific and technical research, international cooperation and sports.

Messi became the first individual football player to be given the honor by the jury, which consists of several members -- including president of the foundation Teresa Perales -- when it was announced in June.

"The truth is that for me it is a great pride to be able to receive this recognition because of the importance it has and for the fact that it is recognized not only for what I do on the pitch but also off the pitch," Messi said when the award was announced.

"I am very happy, and very grateful. I wanted to let you know and send a big hug to everyone. Thank you and see you soon."

Inter Miami currently sits in second place on the Eastern Conference table and secured its place in the 2026 MLS playoffs on Wednesday.

Messi leads MLS' Golden Boot race with 23 goals, four goals ahead of nearest challenger Petar Musa of FC Dallas.

Ahead of the game at the Red Bulls, Miami will visit Atlanta United FC on Saturday.

stories.headline: Lisandro Martínez's Man United comments 'not that far off' but should not have been made - Peter Schmeichel
stories.summary: Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off."
stories.body:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off" but added he would not have liked hearing a teammate sound off in public.

Schmeichel was criticised for his handling of a post-match interview with Martínez in the aftermath of Tuesday night's 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid, when the Argentina defender turned his fire on the club's hierarchy and named director of football Jason Wilcox as one of those from whom he "expects more."

Martínez spoke first to Amazon Prime's Gabriel Clarke before Schmeichel interviewed him for U.S. broadcaster CBS, with the defender repeating many of his criticisms while Schmeichel appeared to be trying to move Martínez on from the topic.

On Thursday Martínez issued a public apology for his comments and United said the matter was considered closed after the 28-year-old met with manager Michael Carrick, Wilcox and the club's hierarchy.

But inevitably the issue dominated Carrick's news conference on Friday with the substance of Martínez's comments still being debated.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Schmeichel said: "I would not like any teammate ever to go out and talk like that. Unless it was Bryan Robson... No, I wouldn't. I absolutely wouldn't like that.

"In the dressing rooms I was in, you were accountable. It just didn't happen very often that somebody stepped out of line, and of course we had a manager [Sir Alex Ferguson] who would not allow you to step out of line. He would react to that straight away...

"It's not that I completely disagree with what [Martínez] says. That's the other thing."

- Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane

Schmeichel then added: "Without going into too much detail about what Martínez said, some of the things he said are not far off.

"Look at the promising teams: Manchester City a long time ago, Arsenal for the past six years, Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp -- what did they do that suddenly changed the dynamics and changed their fortunes? They started at the back.

"They got in a goalkeeper, back four, a centre midfield player. They built that foundation, made it solid, and then they started to bring the creative players in. They've all done it... Built from the back. We've done the opposite, built from the front."

stories.headline: F1 2027 driver lineups: Who has a seat - and who's out of contract?
stories.summary: The 2026 rule changes threw Formula 1 into a new era of challenges and uncertainty, but the real moments of unpredictability are still to come.
stories.body:
The 2026 rule changes threw Formula 1 into a new era of challenges and uncertainty, but the real moments of unpredictability are still to come.

Most drivers secured short-term deals to survive the regulation shift, leaving the grid wide open for the following year. With only a handful of drivers locked into long-term contracts almost every seat on the grid is up for grabs.

Here is our early look at what the future holds for the current Formula 1 lineup.

McLaren

Lando Norris - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2030

Prior to the start of the 2024 F1 season Norris agreed to an "extended multi-year contract beyond 2025."

The reigning champion has now signed a new contract with McLaren until at least 2030. The deal, which includes one of his title-winning Formula 1 cars as a gift from the team, also has the option of a "multi-year" extension beyond 2030.

Oscar Piastri - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2026

Ahead of the first race of the 2025 F1 season Piastri also signed a multi-year contract extension. His previous deal already ran until the end of 2026, and his latest agreement is likely to keep him at McLaren until at least the end of 2028 -- though speculation continues to rumble on about his long-term future.

Ferrari

Lewis Hamilton - 2027

While an exact end date of Hamilton's contract -- signed after completing one of the biggest driver moves in F1 history -- was never officially communicated, Hamilton admitted earlier this year that he still had a contract in place for 2027. That means he got at least a three-year deal at Ferrari, something he had also been seeking at Mercedes.

Amid retirement rumours, Hamilton has also crushed speculation and assured fans that he wasn't going anywhere just yet.

He said: "There's a lot of people that are trying to retire me, and that's not even in my thoughts. I'm already thinking of what will be next, and planning for, like, the next five years. But I still plan to be here for some time."

Charles Leclerc - 2028

Leclerc, who first joined Ferrari in 2019, signed another multi-year extension ahead of the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix.

The team did not publicly reveal an exact expiry date, but the new agreement is understood to take Leclerc to 2028 and potentially beyond, giving Ferrari long-term security over one side of its driver lineup.

Red Bull

Max Verstappen - 2030

Red Bull confirmed in 2022 that four-time world champion Verstappen would remain with the team until the end of 2028 in one of the longest deals on the F1 grid.

Sources told ESPN that performance-related clauses in Verstappen's contract could allow him to leave early, but the Dutchman has now signed a new contract extension with Red Bull until 2030 ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix.

Isack Hadjar - 2027

Isack Hadjar was promoted from Racing Bulls to partner Verstappen for the 2026 season after an impressive rookie campaign. He has now signed a contract extension with Red Bull, securing his seat for the 2027 season.

Mercedes

George Russell - beyond 2026

Russell agreed a new deal with Mercedes ahead of the 2026 season following lengthy negotiations with team principal Toto Wolff.

Although the agreement was initially confirmed as taking him through at least 2026, Russell has since described it as a multi-year deal and said he will fulfill the performance clauses in his contract to stay at Mercedes next year.

Kimi Antonelli - TBC

Mercedes' Antonelli has only been given one-year contracts since his debut, but given his form this season there's no way he'll be leaving the Silver Arrows. Right?

No official announcements have been made yet, but Antonelli could be celebrating both a maiden title and a bumper new deal this year.

Aston Martin

Fernando Alonso - TBC

Alonso's current Aston Martin deal runs until the end of the 2026 season, and he said a decision on his future will come later in the year. At 45 years old, the decision is likely to be between continuing with an underperforming Aston Martin team, or calling time on his F1 career once and for all.

Lance Stroll - TBC

Stroll signed a contract extension in 2024 which kept him with Aston Martin for 2025 "and beyond," but no specific end date was announced. Part of that ambiguity, of course, is because he's the son of team owner Lawrence Stroll.

He remains with the team for 2026, although his position for 2027 has not formally been confirmed.

Alpine

Pierre Gasly - 2028

Gasly is one of the drivers whose future is already settled -- the Frenchman signed a new multi-year agreement with Alpine in 2025 which keeps him locked in at the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

Franco Colapinto - 2027

Colapinto retained his Alpine seat alongside Gasly for 2026 after taking over from Jack Doohan during the previous season. He has now signed a new contract with the team, meaning the Argentinian will continue with Alpine for the 2027 season.

Haas

Rafael Câmara - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2027

F2 star Câmara will replace Esteban Ocon for the 2027 season on a multi-year agreement. The reigning Formula 3 champion and current Formula 2 leader will make his debut in F1 and will partner fellow Ferrari Driver Academy member Oliver Bearman.

Oliver Bearman - TBC

Bearman joined Haas on a multi-year deal when he became a full-time F1 driver in 2025. The exact duration of Bearman's contract has not been made public, leaving his 2027 status uncertain for now.

However, sources with good knowledge of the team's thinking have told ESPN that Bearman is almost certain to stay with the team in 2027 unless a Ferrari seat opens up, then the Englishman remains effectively loaned to Haas.

Racing Bulls

Liam Lawson - TBC

Lawson remained with Racing Bulls for 2026 after rebuilding his season following a short-lived promotion to Red Bull the previous year.

His seat is only confirmed for the current season, meaning the New Zealander will again have to prove his case if he is to stay within the Red Bull set-up in 2027.

Arvid Lindblad - TBC

Lindblad became the latest Red Bull junior to make the jump to Formula 1 when he was handed a Racing Bulls seat for 2026.

The rookie is currently only confirmed for this season and the team have played down speculation over their driver lineup for 2027. You'd be shocked to see him go anywhere, though.

Williams

Carlos Sainz - 'multi-year deal' beyond 2026

Sainz originally joined Williams on a deal covering the 2025 and 2026 seasons, with "options to extend" his stay beyond that. He has recently spoken about wanting to make the Williams project work, leading to him signing a new multi-year extension with the team.

Alex Albon - 2027

Albon signed a new one-year contract with Williams during the summer break, tying him down for the 2027 season. The short-term deal is interesting, given Albon's last contract -- signed in 2024 -- was for multiple years. Keeping those options open?

Audi

Nico Hulkenberg - TBC

Hulkenberg joined Sauber ahead of its transformation into the Audi team on a multi-year contract in 2025.

There are believed to be options in his deal which could allow him to remain with Audi beyond 2026, but an exact end date has not been announced.

Gabriel Bortoleto - TBC

Bortoleto joined Hulkenberg at Sauber before the team's transition to Audi and also signed a multi-year deal.

The Brazilian is contracted through at least the end of 2026, but his place for 2027 has not yet been officially confirmed.

Cadillac

Sergio Perez - 2027

Perez returned to the Formula 1 grid with Cadillac for the team's debut season in 2026 after spending a year away from racing.

The Mexican joined on a multi-year agreement understood to be on similar terms to teammate Valtteri Bottas, putting him in line to remain with Cadillac for 2027.

Valtteri Bottas - 2027

Bottas also returned to a full-time race seat with Cadillac after spending 2025 as Mercedes' reserve driver.

The Finn signed a multi-year deal which runs until at least the end of 2027, giving the new team one of the few already settled driver pairings heading into next season.

stories.headline: UFC champ Alexander Volkanovski proposes 'send-off' superbout vs. Justin Gaethje
stories.summary: UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski is calling for a "send-off" superfight against lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.
stories.body:
UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski has proposed a "send-off" superfight between himself and lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

Volkanovski (28-4) is scheduled to defend his 145-pound title against Movsar Evloev (20-0) at UFC 333 on Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Arguably the greatest featherweight of all time, Volkanovski has acknowledged he is approaching the end of his career at 38 years old. Gaethje, 37, has acknowledged the same since he claimed the UFC's 155-pound title for the first time in June.

With both champions seemingly near the end of their time in the Octagon, Volkanovski has suggested a winner-take-all scenario in 2027.

"Imagine that, do it as a send-off," Volkanovski told the "Who Da Fook Are These Guys?" podcast. "Gaethje, Volk. I think he's said that he maybe has one more. That could be a superfight. Let's do a superfight with the lightweight title on the line. We can both see everyone off with a crazy superfight. That could be really good."

Volkanovski, of Australia, has already tried to capture the lightweight title. He famously challenged then-lightweight champion Islam Makhachev twice in a 10-month span in 2023. He suffered a razor-close decision loss to Makhachev in their first meeting in February then lost by first-round knockout in an October rematch that was scheduled on short notice.

Gaethje (28-5) has not even guaranteed whether he will fight again or retire off his historic win at the White House in June, but he has stated that he believes his next challenger would be lightweight contender Arman Tsarukyan. Volkanovski appears to be throwing his name into the mix in the hope of changing those plans.

"He's said, 'What's the point of doing rematches,'" Volkanovski said. "Let's do a superfight then [retire] straight away after, let the divisions sort themselves out. The UFC would be happy for that. Let's make it happen."

stories.headline: Elias Lindholm's big 3rd period sparks streaking Bruins' comeback for 4-2 win over Ducks
stories.summary: — Elias Lindholm assisted on the tying goal and scored the go-ahead goal in the third period, leading the Boston Bruins past the Anaheim Ducks 4-2 on Friday night for their fourth straight victory.
stories.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. -- — Elias Lindholm assisted on the tying goal and scored the go-ahead goal in the third period, leading the Boston Bruins past the Anaheim Ducks 4-2 on Friday night for their fourth straight victory.


David Pastrnak scored a tying power-play goal and Frederic Brunet got his first NHL goal for the Bruins, who roared back from an early two-goal deficit and improved to 6-2-0.


Less than five minutes after Pastrnak converted a give-and-go with Lindholm, the Ducks failed to mark Lindholm during a power play and allowed him to tap in a pass from Pavel Zacha with 11:39 to play. Matthew Poitras added another goal with 3:40 left on James Hagens' second assist of the night.


Michael DiPietro made 25 saves in his second start of the season for the Bruins.


Beckett Sennecke got his fifth goal and Tim Washe also scored for the Ducks, who have lost three straight home games while giving up 13 goals. Lukas Dostal stopped 18 shots.


Ducks captain Mikael Granlund sat out with an upper-body injury, and goal-scoring winger Cutter Gauthier filled in by moving to center for the first time in his NHL career.


Anaheim had the best chances in the first period, and it took a lead with two goals 20 seconds apart in the final minute. After Washe's long shot went in through the legs of screening teammate Jeff Malott, Sennecke finished a strong passing sequence with Gauthier and Nikita Nesterenko.


Brunet trimmed Anaheim's lead with his first goal early in the second, connecting on a power play in the 23-year-old defenseman's sixth NHL game.


After the Ducks failed to score on a four-minute power play, Pastrnak's 423rd career goal broke a tie with Brad Marchand for the fourth-most in Bruins history.


The Ducks have sold out Honda Center for the first four games of a new season for the first time since 2007, when the team was coming off its lone Stanley Cup title.

Ducks: At New York Rangers on Monday.

stories.headline: Titans CEO apologizes to fans, supports Robert Saleh, GM
stories.summary: Titans CEO Burke Nihill said the organization believes that coach Robert Saleh and GM Mike Borgonzi are "ultimately going to get this team out of the woods."
stories.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Titans CEO Burke Nihill, who is empowered to speak on behalf of controlling owner Amy Adams-Strunk, said the organization fully believes in coach Robert Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi and will have patience with them.

The Titans are 0-5 in Saleh's first season as coach and have won only three games since Borgonzi joined the team prior to the 2025 season. Overall, the franchise has won just six games dating to the 2023 season.

"I personally feel a sense of stability," Nihill told ESPN on Friday. "I believe that Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh are ultimately going to get this team out of the woods and restore it to competitive football. The train is on the tracks. It just hasn't picked up momentum, but it will.

"I can confidently say this organization is in a place where there is organizational belief in Mike, in Robert, and they absolutely have all the support they need to get this train moving and moving faster."

Saleh's first season in Tennessee has not gotten off to a good start. The defense has generated only two turnovers, and the offense is averaging a league-low 246.4 yards and 11.6 points.

Regardless, Saleh said the Titans are sticking to their process, which he described as "rigorous and detailed," and vowed to put their best foot forward on Sundays.

"We're going through a lot of adversity," Saleh said. "But if we capture it the right way, we're going to find a lot of growth, and when I tell you guys that the sun is going to shine on this organization eventually, it's going to shine."

The Titans have fired a coach or general manager every year since 2022. They recently fired senior vice president of brand marketing Erin Swartz, senior vice president and chief revenue officer Adam Nuse and vice president of creative Charles Jensen.

When asked about the instability, Nihill said it's possible to be "agile while still being stable as a business."

Tennessee has lost 33 of its past 39 games and is stuck in a seven-game losing streak dating to Week 17 of last season. There was a lot of optimism that the Titans would take a big step toward respectability heading into the opening of Nissan Stadium next season, but a poor product has left many fans wondering when they will get another win.

"The first thing I would say back to the fans is just that we're sorry," Nihill told ESPN. "There's nobody in this building that doesn't feel ... a sense of grief about it, because not only are we fans of the team as well, but we feel the sense of responsibility to deliver. And we've let our fans down because football is supposed to be fun.

"I think it starts on the field and the state of the franchise. We're 0-5, and that's not nearly good enough. It hasn't been for a while."

stories.headline: Xabi Alonso not ready to say if Chelsea heading 'right way'
stories.summary: Xabi Alonso said it is too early to tell whether Chelsea are going the "right way" as he looks for greater balance from his free-scoring team.
stories.body:
Xabi Alonso said it is too early to tell whether Chelsea are going the "right way" as he looks for greater balance from his free-scoring team.

A chaotic start to life under the Spanish coach sees the Blues sit as the third-highest scorers in the Premier League with 15 goals from their six games, yet no team in the division has conceded more than their 13.

- Alonso: Reece James may be out beyond Christmas

- Ranked: Who are the best 50 players in the Premier League so far this season?

- Moisés Caicedo determined to repay Alonso's faith

In total there have been 28 goals scored in Chelsea's league games so far with six more coming in last weekend's 5-1 win over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

"You need a lot of clean sheets to win trophies," Alonso said. "But you need to score a lot of goals. So it's about being strong in defence, being good in attack and we are in that process.

"We are still early days. This first part we've been doing good things, other things to be improved. To do a very deep analysis, it's too early probably.

"In February we will have enough game to see where we are going and if it's the right way. But we are demanding in terms of what we are doing and what we can do better."

Much of the issue in conceding goals has come from a lack of control in midfield, a problem that appeared largely to have been fixed on Saturday as Moisés Caicedo made his first start of the season.

The return of the Ecuador midfielder after a calf injury brought far greater stability in the middle of the pitch, with Jordan Henderson, who scored his first two goals for the club as the Cherries were routed, also influential alongside him.

The pair are likely to be used together more than had been planned in the coming weeks with Reece James likely to be out until the new year after undergoing what the club called "minor" surgery on a knee problem.

"It's one game, but we saw positives," Alonso said. "Moises helps Hendo, Hendo helps Moises. I think as well Rom [Roméo] Lavia is in a good moment. He played 25 minutes and he did really well. We need not just two midfielders, we need more than that.

"In terms of personalities, they match well. Hendo he has this energy, he is very active, he covers a lot of pitch. He finds a balance with Moisés who is more in position, he has this stability to be in good distances with everything.

"It was a good start and we need to keep building from that."

Chelsea travel to face Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday knowing that a win will take them above David Moyes' side, with both teams currently on 10 points from six matches.

stories.headline: Harry Kane has talent for NFL - Jags kicker Cam Little
stories.summary: Cam Little is confident Harry Kane has the skill to become an NFL kicker.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Cam Little is confident Harry Kane has the skill to become an NFL kicker.

But the hard part for Kane, the Jacksonville Jaguars kicker said, would be shifting from star striker to bit player.

"I think the transition from soccer to football is so much more cultural than like the actual skill," Little said.

The England captain and Bayern Munich forward has mused over the years about one day kicking in the NFL. He recently floated the idea of combining his NFL goal with also joining an MLS team.

Who better to weigh in than Little? The soccer player-turned kicker, who remains a diehard Manchester United fan, booted a 57-yard field goal as time expired for the Jags to defeat the Philadelphia Eagles 19-17 last Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. He also holds the record for longest NFL field goal -- 68 yards.

"It's just so different," Little told The Associated Press of moving from being involved in a game for 90 minutes to being a kicker "sitting there on the sidelines the whole game.

"You're not going to get on the ball, and you don't have the same moxie, I guess, because he is a star striker for the team. So that moxie is just kind of put to the side. You've got to let everyone else do the big man's job, and then you're out there just to back everyone up basically."

As far as Kane's ability, "he's probably talented enough to do it ... His technique in soccer is so good. But it's just such a different mental, I'd say, challenge than soccer.

"It'd be like him taking five set pieces a day. And he's got to deliver on all five set pieces, or you didn't do your job for the day," Little said Thursday after practice at the team's accommodations north of London in Watford.

"So, it's just a lot different, but I don't think he doesn't have the talent level for it. I think he probably has the skill to do it."

Little and the Jaguars remained in London this week ahead of the game against the Houston Texans on Sunday at Wembley Stadium.

Little, a sixth-round draft pick from Arkansas in 2024, had missed an extra-point attempt -- after a high snap from fill-in long snapper DaVon Hamilton -- late in the fourth quarter against the Eagles. The miss had looked crucial because Philadelphia then took a 17-16 lead with just 8 seconds left -- before the improbable ending on Little's heroics.

"Missing a set piece or missing a wide-open goal, you see a lot of strikers do that, and they'll come back and put the game away," Little said at his post-game news conference while wearing a Man United jersey. "I've got to have short-term memory and be at my best when the best is required."

Little told AP that he'd be attending Fulham's home game against Hull at Craven Cottage on Saturday. Jaguars owner Shad Khan also owns the Premier League club.

Little, an Oklahoma native, played as a midfielder before switching to American football in high school. England and United great Wayne Rooney was his favorite player.

"Maybe one day I'll get to meet him or do a jersey swap with him. That's my goal," he said. "I've never been to Manchester. Only London, but I'm hoping to make it there this offseason."

stories.headline: Shakhtar's Champions League win vs. AEK was more than just a game
stories.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk haven't played at home since 2014 due to the war, and this season, their Champions League home games are at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Wednesday's win was a reminder of how absurd their situation is.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Take a step back and revel in the absurdity for a minute. Shakhtar Donetsk, a Ukrainian team from the Russian-speaking part of the country, are playing a Greek team, AEK Athens, in London, at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Technically, it's a "home game," but that concept has become rather meaningless.

Shakhtar haven't played at their home, the Donbas Arena, since May 2014, some 650 weeks ago. They turn up wherever someone will host them: Odessa, Kyiv, Kharkiv and Lviv for Ukrainian league games; Warsaw, Hamburg, Gelsenkirchen, Krakow, Ljubljana and now London for matches in European competition. Why? Because their opponents can't (or won't) travel to Ukraine, where none of the civilian airports are open, air raid sirens go off a dozen times a day, and where drones and bombs can't be trusted to distinguish between a military captain and the captain of a soccer team.

It's pretty obvious that in those circumstances, you're more than a club -- you're a symbol of defiance, an attempt to maintain some sort of normality in the face of a war that has taken more than half a million lives and displaced tens of millions more.

"We are playing for people from Ukraine all over the world," sporting director Dario Srna said. "Everywhere we've gone, they've come [to see us]. We represent Ukraine in the center of the world: we're not just playing for us. [We are] a Ukrainian team, we are not just Shakhtar."

But, of course, nothing is normal. Everything is messed up, and their mere presence in the Champions League constitutes a political dimension.

Wednesday night, Shakhtar were at Stamford Bridge, the home of Chelsea. Resourceful as ever, street vendors outside the ground hawked their off-brand scarves, except rather than "Cole Palmer," "João Pedro" and "John Terry," the names read "Pedrinho," "[Mykola] Matviyenko" and "[Valeriy] Bondar." Watching over them was a life-size cardboard cutout of Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, only his face was replaced by that of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelenskyy.

Inside, visiting AEK fans -- who turned the Shed End into a two-tier wall of tifo, flags and noise -- outsing, if not outnumber, the "home" support.

Because yes, this is Shakhtar's home for the Champions League this season, a move made possible by the London club's failure to qualify for European competitions (and, probably, a need to rake in some extra rent on those empty weeknights). Ironically, Chelsea's previous owner, Roman Abramovich, was forced by the U.K. government to sell the club after the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, because of his ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Abramovich holds passports from Portugal, Israel and Russia. His yachts are moored in Turkey.

Abramovich, whose mother is Ukrainian, is a complicated figure. So is Shakhtar's version of Abramovich, Rinat Akhmetov.

An ethnic Russian, but Donetsk-born and bred, Akhmetov's huge wealth from mining and energy bankrolled the club's rise to prominence prewar -- lest we forget, the likes of Willian and Fernandinho, Henrikh Mkiytaryan and Douglas Costa are all Shakhtar alums -- and keeps it alive and very much kicking today. Forbes estimates his wealth at nearly $8 billion and like most folks of that ilk, Akhmetov could easily have made different choices, decamping abroad. When the war broke out, he chose to stay, and that was not something to take for granted, given that he had previously clashed with Zelenskyy and, in the 2000s, served in parliament in the party of former pro-Russian Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych, whom he also backed financially.

Akhmetov broke with Yanukovych in 2014 and while his pro-Ukrainian words today are loud, his actions -- from staying in the country to tirelessly campaigning to his efforts with Shakhtar -- speak even louder.

"He can't leave Ukraine, not after seeing what he has seen," Srna says of Akhmetov. "It's impossible. He's devoted himself to this, helping the economy, helping the people. All while sleeping each night under bombs."

Many Ukrainians have no choice, which makes the actions of those who could be elsewhere all the more remarkable. It takes an unconventional type of person.

Most of Shakhtar's players are Brazilian -- lured by money, sure, but also the opportunity to showcase their talent. The coach, former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona standout Arda Turan, is Turkish. Even if you don't remember what he was like as a player, watching him prowl the technical area during the AEK game, fists clenched and eyes wild, you come to understand how this is the same guy who once got into an altercation with a pop star in an Istanbul hospital.

Srna himself is Croatian, but has been at the club -- first as a player then as sporting director -- for 23 years. He too could have left umpteen times and, in fact, he says he even turned down the chance to take over Barcelona's recruitment a decade ago.

"Ukraine and Shakhtar are in my blood," he says. "If I leave now, I couldn't live with myself."

In some ways, Srna has been here before. He was eight years old when civil war broke out in the former Yugoslavia in March 1991. The conflict that would rage for 4½ years, ripped apart communities along ethnic lines. Neighbors took up arms against neighbors. His own father woke up every day supplying baked goods for the military. If you've seen the ESPN 30 for 30 documentary "Once Brothers" about the relationship between Drazen Petrovic and Vlade Divac, well ... he lived it. Twice. Maybe that's why he soldiers on, numb to what he is experiencing.

"I have this feeling inside myself," he says. "It's a feeling I felt before [as a child experiencing war in Croatia]. But when you feel that pain and it comes back to you again, well, you're not going to have the same pain twice. I know this pain. I know this feeling ..."

Srna trails off as he searches for the right words of history -- the worst parts -- repeating itself with him in the middle of it. But then he flickers back with righteous anger.

"This is unbelievable, I can't explain it," he says. "Four-and-a-half years [this war has continued]. Bombing each other, destroying everything ... for what? For f---ing what? People die, families are destroyed, children are traumatized and grow up with psychological problems ..."

On this Wednesday night, even as Shakhtar emerge as 3-1 victors over AEK, you're reminded once again of the difficulties. The team were up at 6 a.m. on Thursday to catch a 10 o'clock flight on a plane they chartered from a budget airline taking them back to Rzeszow in Poland. They'll then board a bus back across the border into Ukraine, arriving -- best-case scenario -- at 9 p.m. local time. All this not knowing whether they'll have power and heat when they arrive, or whether they'll be making regular trips into the air raid shelter.

You want to end on a note of hope. Srna does his best to offer it, but he clearly isn't going to lie to you or to himself.

"We [Croatians] have more or less an OK relationship now with Serbia," he says. "Time [30 years have passed] is helping, generations change, it's different people. We take a step back and understand what was good, what was not good. We can't say all Serbian people are bad ... But in this moment, it's not possible to be friends with a Russian person. In time, maybe a few years, maybe many years, I don't know ... right now though, it's impossible."

Certainly more impossible than a club without a home in a country at war defying logic and competing in the Champions League against the likes of Real Madrid, who visit Stamford Bridge on Jan. 27.

One of the side effects of war is the normalization of the horrific and the absurd. Shakhtar's plight has, by necessity, normalized the absurd, in an effort to stave off the horrific.

stories.headline: AFL trade and free agency grades - Every club's report card from the 2026 transfer period
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is over. Some teams improved, some stagnated, and others, well, got worse. Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is complete. Some teams improved, some have stagnated, and others, well, seemed to have gotten worse.

READ: Every player move from the 2026 off-season

Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks:

Adelaide
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Jordon Butts, Luke Pedlar

2026 draft selections: 15, 32, 35, 43, 56, 92

I'm not sure what the Crows' gameplan was this trade and free agency period, but it's fair to say the club sat on its hands and did next to nothing. Losing key defender Jordon Butts to the Bulldogs obviously weakens them, while just one draft selection inside the top 30 is unlikely to provide much immediate support. Adelaide's list profile remains fine, and maybe they will surprise us all in 2027, but you just get the sense so many other clubs have passed them by over the last two weeks.

Grade: F

Brisbane
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Lachie Neale, Sam Marshall, Will McLachlan, Keidean Coleman

2026 draft selections: 21, 27, 28, 45, 79, 97

The Lions were the biggest winners of last year's off-season (and season!), but this year was a different story. All year it seemed a formality they would lose the services of dual Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale, who ultimately signed with Collingwood as a free agent. They also waved goodbye to Keidean Coleman and Sam Marshall, two players who had struggled to crack the best 23 of late. No picks inside the top 20 would be concerning for 17 other clubs, but the Lions still have so much young talent at their disposal and are primed to challenge again in 2027.

Grade: C-

Carlton
Incoming: Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield

Outgoing: Hudson O'Keeffe, Flynn Riley

2026 draft selections: 13, 18, 31, 50, 61, 72, 90

The Blues addressed two areas of weakness this off-season. The addition of free agent Joel Amartey provides spearhead Harry McKay with a stable forward line partner, while the Lachie Whitfield signing offers run, experience, and a kick-first option off halfback, the perfect piece to fit into Josh Fraser's system. Carlton really didn't give up much to land Whitfield, either. And barring Essendon taking a stab at talented father-son prospect Cody Walker with pick No. 1, the club has also ensured it has enough draft capital to match any bids that will come for him.

Grade: A

Collingwood
Incoming: Lachie Neale, Jesse Hogan, Flynn Riley

Outgoing: Scott Pendlebury

2026 draft selections: 11, 30, 67, 68, 70, 88

The Magpies had been crying out for a true inside midfielder, and they landed arguably the best in the competition in Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow Medal winner is an elite ball winner and clearance player, and should perfectly complement superstar Nick Daicos. Collingwood also signed Jesse Hogan, a man that won the Coleman Medal just two years ago, and gave up virtually nothing for him. The loss of champion Scott Pendlebury obviously stings, but you have to feel this club is in a stronger position now than it was two weeks ago.

Grade: A

Essendon
Incoming: Jack Bowes, Keidean Coleman

Outgoing: Zach Merrett, Jordan Ridley

2026 draft selections: 1, 17, 25, 80

Former skipper Zach Merrett finally got his wish of a fresh start at the Hawks, while fellow experienced player Jordan Ridley also departs the club for the Cats. The additions of Jack Bowes and Keidean Coleman are fine, but are either going to be difference makers in a side that's been languishing at the bottom of the ladder for several years? I'm not so sure. The only saving grace for the Bombers is that they hold pick No. 1. They simply have to make the most of that selection.

Grade: D

Fremantle
Incoming: Dom Bedendo

Outgoing: Nathan O'Driscoll

2026 draft selections: 19, 40, 60, 63, 78, 96

The Dockers were incredibly quiet during the trade and free agency window, but that's not exactly a bad thing. Remember, if not for Will Ashcroft and Logan Morris, Fremantle win the 2026 premiership. There was absolutely no reason for the Dockers to panic and overpay for someone after their Grand Final heartbreak, instead, this club, with its plethora of youth and talent, should feel as if it can contend for years to come. Trust the process and go again in 2027.

Grade: C

Geelong
Incoming: Toby Greene, Jordan Ridley, Rowan Marshall

Outgoing: Jack Bowes

2026 draft selections: 36, 57, 62, 75, 93

Every year the Cats just find a way to bring big names through the door, and 2026 was no exception. Rowan Marshall was tipped to join 12 months ago and finally makes the move from St Kilda to bolster the club's ruck stocks. Toby Greene adds class, experience, and unrivalled goal-kicking nous to the forward line. Jordan Ridley is a stable and still wildly underrated defensive asset. The best part? To land this trio the club only had to give up midfield depth piece Jack Bowes, and some draft capital. They won't be much of a feature at the upcoming draft, but they don't have to be. These Cats are in win-now mode.

Grade: A

Gold Coast Suns
Incoming: Scott Pendlebury, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler

Outgoing: Ben King

2026 draft selections: 8, 85

Scott Pendlebury might be a champion of the game, but there's no denying the Suns just got worse. The addition of 38-year-old Pendlebury doesn't outweigh the seismic loss of spearhead Ben King, a man who has booted 230 goals over the last four seasons. How do they replace him? Perhaps it's the incoming Aidan Schubert, but he's years away from having a real impact. Making matters worse, it seems Brownlow medallist Matt Rowell is likely to request a trade back to Victoria at the end of next season. This club is in a real precarious spot right now. A penny for Christian Petracca's thoughts...

Grade: C-

GWS Giants
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield

2026 draft selections: 9, 20, 26, 59, 77, 86

Just two years ago Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, and Lachie Whitfield were probably four of the Giants' most important players. None of them remain at the club after an action-packed trade and free agency window, with GWS instead opting to clear out and trust the youth underneath. It's a move that will either make the Giants look like geniuses or total fools, but even those who are incredibly bullish about the approach would concede there is likely to be some pain on the immediate horizon.

Grade: D

Hawthorn
Incoming: Zach Merrett, Ben King, Josh Goater

Outgoing: Finn Maginness, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler, Bodie Ryan

2026 draft selections: 29, 37, 71, 94

The Hawks should probably be the 2027 flag favourites after a whirlwind two weeks that's seen them finally land former Essendon skipper Zach Merrett, as well as Ben King. Merrett adds depth, experience, and A-grade ball use to Hawthorn's midfield group, while King provides a focal point in attack, taking the burden off the ageing Jack Gunston. Sure, Hawthorn gave up some depth, but their best 23 has improved out of sight and they still have draft collateral over the next few years to ensure talent keeps coming through the door.

Grade: A+

Melbourne
Incoming: Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, Bodie Ryan

Outgoing: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

2026 draft selections: 4, 14, 48, 52

Just about everyone panicked when the Demons farewelled premiership heroes Christian Petracca and Clayton Oliver last year, and look how that turned out. This club seems to have a plan for the future and it isn't prepared to compromise on what it wants. Melbourne has nailed its draft picks in recent times and with selections four and 14 this year, you'd expect two more highly talented prospects to join the ranks. Who knows if Zane Duursma will work out, but they've landed him for a fraction of what the Kangaroos gave up at the draft three years ago. It's a low risk punt worth taking.

Grade: C

North Melbourne
Incoming: Nick Blakey

Outgoing: Zane Duursma, Josh Goater

2026 draft selections: 33, 49, 66, 74, 84

Credit to the Kangaroos, they finally landed a big name. The only problem is I'm not sure Nick Blakey is the superstar many are claiming. There's no doubt Blakey will add drive and dash off halfback, but is he the player you look to in the closing stages of a tight game? North also gave up a truckload of future draft capital to get him through the door which will hurt them in the coming years. And then there's the Zane Duursma fiasco. Losing a player the club invested pick No. 4 in just three years ago is an unmitigated disaster. With no selections inside the top 30 this year, it will be a rare draft without the Roos being a major player.

Grade: C+

Port Adelaide
Incoming: Luke Pedlar

Outgoing: Zak Butters

2026 draft selections: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46, 65

You're never going to feel great when a player of Zak Butters' class and calibre walks out the door, but the silver lining for Port Adelaide is that Dougie Cochrane should be set to walk back in. The academy talent is the consensus best player in the upcoming draft and the Power are in a position to match any bids on their man. Expect Port to be heavily involved in the draft over the next couple of years as they look to rebuild around the likes of Cochrane, Connor Rozee, and Jason Horne-Francis.

Grade: B

Richmond
Incoming: Kieren Briggs, Nathan O'Driscoll

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 2, 5, 44, 81

The Tigers found Toby Nankervis' successor in Kieren Briggs, who crosses from the Giants as a free agent. That's a nice win. Nathan O'Driscoll was unable to find a place in Fremantle's best team of late but should receive far more opportunity in the black and yellow jumper in 2027. Richmond has two more picks inside the top five, though they are likely to be shuffled down a few spots with bid matching on Dougie Cochrane and Cody Walker, and they simply must nail them. Even still, this side will remain incredibly young in 2027.

Grade: C

St Kilda
Incoming: Sam Marshall

Outgoing: Rowan Marshall

2026 draft selections: 10, 16, 41, 51, 69, 87

The Saints went all-in last year, signing Tom De Koning, Jack Silvagni, Liam Ryan, and Sam Flanders. They weren't nearly as busy this off-season, and few expected them to be. Long-time ruck Rowan Marshall departs the club for the Cats, while Sam Marshall joins and should bolster their midfield stocks. Outside of that, St Kilda will be hoping to cash in with their two first round draft selections. If not, it could spell the end of Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera's tenure. This team wouldn't want to be starting 2027 slowly...

Grade: C

Sydney Swans
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Joel Amartey, Nick Blakey

2026 draft selections: 6, 38, 39, 47, 54, 76, 95

Two best 23 players departed the Swans this past fortnight with halfback Nick Blakey being traded to the Kangaroos and key forward Joel Amartey signing with the Blues as a free agent. Don't forget, Callum Mills is unlikely to suit up for the entire year after suffering an ACL injury during this year's finals campaign. That's three best 23 players to replace! Who knows what's happening with Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner? Swans fans will be praying for a hit with pick No. 6 at the upcoming draft to soften the blow.

Grade: C-

West Coast Eagles
Incoming: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 3, 23, 58, 64, 73, 82

It's clear the Eagles don't want to take the same approach as the Tigers and rely solely on the kids. Instead, they're continuing to add experienced pieces around their young talent in an effort to ease the rebuild and avoid a nosedive in morale. Jack Viney and Trent Rivers add premiership experience to the club and they haven't had to give up too much to get them. West Coast will feature prominently at November's draft with pick No. 3, 23, as well as a compensation pick in the likely scenario that the club's first selection is pushed back by a bid.

Grade: C+

Western Bulldogs
Incoming: Jordon Butts, Finn Maginness, Hudson O'Keeffe, Zak Butters

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 42, 53, 55, 83, 89, 91

The Bulldogs now possess the most dynamic midfield trio in the game with Zak Butters joining skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards in the red, white, and blue. It's a marquee signing for Luke Beveridge's team that simply has to put them into premiership contention. Jordon Butts also joins the club and will bolster what's traditionally been a weaker defensive unit. Don't forget about key forward star Sam Darcy, who will return from a season-ending ACL injury.

Grade: A+

stories.headline: Why is Max Verstappen racing in GT World Challenge? Schedule, how to watch latest non-F1 event
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has made no secret of his enjoyment of racing outside Formula 1, and the four-time world champion is set to take on his latest motorsport challenge.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has made no secret of his enjoyment of racing outside Formula 1, and the four-time world champion is set to take on his latest racing challenge.

There is little time for rest for the Dutchman, who heads to Portimão to compete in the latest GT World Challenge event, sandwiched between two F1 triple-headers.

The one-off event will also feature some of the best drivers in the world, including World Endurance Championship title winner Nicki Thiim, nine-time MotoGP world champion Valentino Rossi, who competes for BMW in the World Endurance Championship, and Ferrari development driver Arthur Leclerc.

Here's everything you need to know about the 10th and final round of the GT World Challenge.

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

- When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

Why is Verstappen racing this weekend?

Verstappen has been one of the biggest critics around F1's controversial new regulations, calling them "anti-racing."

Things are, however, on the up after he took his first victory this season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, before following it up with a dominant win in Singapore, as Red Bull continue to thrive with its upgraded package.

Despite finding success in F1, the simple reason why he's back to GT racing this weekend is due to some of Verstappen Racing's usual drivers not being available to compete. Dani Juncadella and Jules Gounon have a World Endurance Championship calendar clash with the Portuguese round on Oct. 18.

Verstappen decided to step in and will be racing alongside Ben Barnicoat and Chris Lulham.

"I know that two of my drivers won't be part of the line-up, so two other drivers need to step in and I'm looking forward to it," Verstappen said.

"It's going to be a busy seven weeks, but we'll do it and I enjoy it anyway. So, yeah. Let's see what we can do there."

It's set to be a busy weekend with the GT2 European Series, GT4 European Series and McLaren Trophy Europe all set to crown their champions.

The 29-year-old will be back in his Red Bull a week later in Texas for F1's United States Grand Prix, where he will target a third win in a row.

GT World Challenge schedule
All times in BST

Thursday, October 15

Official Paid Test Session 1: 11.50 a.m.

Bronze test: 5.40 p.m.

Friday, October 16

Free Practice 1: 8.45 a.m.

Qualifying: 5.55 p.m. - 7.05 p.m.

Saturday, October 17

Race: 5 p.m. - 8 p.m.

How to watch

The GT World Challenge will be streamed on the official GT World YouTube Channel or via the GT World Challenge Europe website.

Portimão Circuit

Built in the Algarve region in southern Portugal, the circuit is a mix of fast and slow corners which features some extreme elevation changes.

There are overtaking opportunities, but the 4.653km track is considered challenging with its 16 corners.

It's so popular that it's returning to the F1 calendar in 2027 and 2028. The race next year will take the place of the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort.

Weather forecast

The weather forecast for the race in Portimão is set to be sunny with a gentle breeze, with highs of 27°C on Thursday through to race day on Saturday.

Verstappen's other racing ventures

During his debut GT3 race in the Nürburgring Endurance Series in September last year he landed a stunning victory in a Ferrari 296 entered by Emil Frey Racing.

In March, he drove a Mercedes-AMG GT3 through Verstappen Racing in the preliminary NLS2 race which is a four-hour endurance race. He won the race but was later disqualified over a tyre error.

A few months later he competed in one of motor racing's toughest endurance tests -- the iconic Nürburgring 24-hour race under Verstappen Racing driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3 Evo.

He came close to ticking a dream off his list, but his car suffered a driveshaft issue with three hours of the race remaining.

Verstappen more recently took part in a more lighthearted challenge where he took on 100 creators and sports personalities in go-karts starting from the back of the grid. Nobody was sure how the race would unravel at the custom-built track at Silverstone, but he ended up passing every single driver to lead the race after 35 minutes.

stories.headline: Michael 'Venom' Page: UFC's Dana White 'never really a fan of me'
stories.summary: Michael "Venom" Page has said that his relationship with UFC president Dana White was "nonexistent."
stories.body:
Michael "Venom" Page said that his relationship with UFC president Dana White was "nonexistent" in an exclusive interview with ESPN on Tuesday.

Page joined the UFC in 2023 with his stock at an all-time high after serving as the face of Bellator courtesy of a series of exciting stoppages with his unique freestyle striking style.

But he couldn't replicate that in the UFC with a run of impressive, albeit uninspiring, decision wins in the promotion, along with a solitary defeat to Ian Machado-Garry, leading to the conclusion of his six-fight contract.

White confirmed in September that the UFC would not pursue another deal, and Page announced this week that his next venture is with KSI's Misfits boxing in a "multi-fight, multi-year agreement." And reflecting on his time in the promotion, Page said he felt that White was "never really a fan of me from the beginning."

"Literally nonexistent [relationship with White]," Page told ESPN. "I think we've had a couple of very brief conversations, very, very brief. [Chief business officer Hunter Campbell] was the person that I spoke with quite regularly. I was thankful for him. ... It was him that signed me. It was more Hunter that was the person that was like, 'Look, I want you in the UFC.'

"So I feel like Dana White's never really been a fan of me from the beginning, or I think it came from somebody else. And because I also didn't deliver it in the way he wanted me to deliver, I get he didn't care. You can kind of tell from the announcement, he didn't really make anything of it. He just announced me on the card as if I've always been a fighter there and people were kind of like, 'Wait, what?'

"So I feel like potentially, just based on how he behaves, I'm speculating here, that potentially he wasn't necessarily a fan of mine. And then on top of that, I didn't give him what he wanted as well. So yeah, there was no real relationship with Dana."

UFC didn't respond to ESPN's request for comment.

Page's UFC career wrapped up with a decision win over Nursulton Ruziboev amid boos from a partisan crowd in Paris last month.

Misfits wasn't the only promotion Page spoke to when looking at steps after the UFC with Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions among those interested in the Brit. Page said that a move to MVP, who has recently acquired MMA promotion PFL, was considered, but the timing wasn't right.

"Obviously that [MVP] was probably one of the things at the top of the list. But they just weren't in the right place right now," he said. "It wasn't the right timing more than anything. It wasn't just a financial thing, but it wasn't the right timing for them."

stories.headline: Judge sides with NRL over NZ Rugby on Chiefs name
stories.summary: Rugby league has struck the first blow in the Chief name wars, with New Zealand Rugby's urgent injunction denied ahead of the new PNG NRL club's jersey reveal.
stories.body:
New Zealand's High Court has knocked back an application for an interim injunction on the PNG Chiefs NRL franchise using its name in the country.

New Zealand Rugby (NZR) had rushed to court ahead of the PNG team's logo and jersey reveal in Port Moresby next week.

The organisation claimed use of the Chiefs name, also the name of the long-standing Super Rugby Pacific outfit, would cause confusion and damage to the brand value.

But a judge at Friday's two-hour Wellington hearing turned down the application after hearing an injunction could harm the NRL expansion outfit's efforts to attract players ahead of a 2028 debut.

The dispute remains though, with the application for a final injunction still before the court and legal action in Australia a consideration.

ARLC executive chairman Peter V'landys last week labelled NZR's action one of "mind-blowing hypocrisy", using the example of the Auckland Blues' arrival decades after the NSW Blues "had been the Blues".

"Today's decision is not a judgement on the strength of our case, and the matter will still be heard in full," NZR boss Steve Lancaster said.

"As the trademark holder, our responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand hasn't changed. We remain open to working with the ARLC on a solution."

NZR's lawyer Earl Gray argued on Friday that the PNG Chiefs' use of 'PNG Chiefs' and 'Chiefs' interchangeably created confusion for fans of both codes and that, with no clear distinction between the two, it would strip the rugby Chiefs' brand exclusivity.

He said NZR had trademark protections for the Chiefs in New Zealand that the NRL had not acknowledged.

ARLC laywer Clive Elliot argued that the request for an urgent injunction, about a year after NZR became aware of the PNG Chiefs name, was not appropriate.

He said an injunction now would cloud the franchise's reputation ahead of a recruitment blitz once free agency opens in November.
